Main Points
⏺ A watch-only wallet lets users monitor balances and transactions without holding private keys
⏺ This setup is useful for large portfolios, cold storage, and address analysis
⏺ This post explains why monitoring assets doesn't require spending access

1️⃣ Core Idea — the app receives a public wallet address and displays its assets and transaction history.
2️⃣ Why It Helps — users can monitor long-term holdings without connecting the device that stores their private keys.
3️⃣ Use Cases — cold wallets, corporate treasuries, whale monitoring, and crypto portfolio accounting.
4️⃣ Risk Surface — the app cannot sign transactions without a key, but it may collect information about your addresses and financial activity.
5️⃣ Practical Rule — add only public addresses, verify supported networks, and never enter a seed phrase just to view balances.


Final Thoughts

You don't need to give an app control over your crypto just to monitor it. Separating viewing from signing reduces situations where private keys are exposed to unnecessary risk.

🔬 Capacity Deep-Dive #1: SOL/BTC (With Live Proof)

SOL is one of the most heavily traded assets on Earth, racking up $2.4 Billion in global volume over the last 24 hours. Because the SOL↔️BTC pair moves constantly across dozens of global venues, it represents textbook arbitrage. Every single micro-movement is an opportunity automated bots actively want to capture.

Theory is great, but production numbers are better. The GalaSwap SOL/BTC pool now exists, and because it is young and lean, it is performing exceptionally well.

### 📊 The Live Dashboard Snapshot (July 7)

GSOL / GWBTC (0.3% Fee Tier)

* Pool Depth: Just $26,000
* 30-Day Volume: $7.57 Million
* Daily Velocity: The pool turns over its entire depth ~9.5× every single day.
* Annualized Yield: ~262% APR *(based on yesterday's single-day fee snapshot).*

Let those numbers sink in: a tiny $26k pool routed $7.5M in a single month. This is the exact "early window" phenomenon in action—a small pool catching the full force of a massive, external arbitrage firehose.

---

### 📉 The Compression Curve In Action

As a pool grows and matures, its yield naturally stabilizes. You can see this live curve playing out right now across GalaSwap’s 0.3% fee tier pools:

* $26k Depth (SOL/BTC) ➡️ ~262% APR
* $160k Depth (SOL/ETH) ➡️ ~126% APR
* $866k Depth (BTC/ETH) ➡️ ~37% APR

This is our entire capacity thesis wrapped into three live data points: as liquidity depth grows, the rate cools. But notice how yields remain in the double digits even at nearly $1M in depth. Why? Because the volume is driven by external global market volatility, not by the size of our pool.

---

### 🚀 Where is the Ceiling?

How much liquidity can the SOL/BTC pool actually hold before compressing to ordinary DeFi rates?

The model indicates the ceiling is set by that massive $2.4B/day external market. Assuming a conservative 5% capture rate at the 0.3% fee tier, this single pool could productively absorb tens of millions of dollars in liquidity.

Today, it holds just $26k—roughly 0.1% of its implied capacity.

The Big Picture: One major trading pair, a pool turning over 9.5× daily, and a runway that is three orders of magnitude larger than its current size. Now consider that the GalaSwap grid has hundreds of pairs waiting to be built—some deeper, some hotter, and most still completely untouched.

SOL/BTC isn't just a proof of concept anymore. It’s the live demo. 🟡

Good morning! I’m on my way to London Heathrow to catch my flight home to Tel Aviv.

During my Sunday evening message in Catania, Sicily, exactly a week ago today, the Lord brought something to my attention that wasn’t in my notes: even during the millennial kingdom, when Jesus Himself will rule over the nations and David will reign over Israel, the human heart will still need to be changed (Revelation 20:4–6; Ezekiel 37:24–25).

We live in a fallen world, yet we often expect our political leaders to be perfect. When they disappoint us, we sometimes refuse to vote altogether - as though our absence will somehow make things better.

We also judge leaders by their unfulfilled promises without considering the opposition, obstruction, and resistance they face in trying to fulfill them.

But consider this: even after a thousand years under the righteous reign of Jesus, Satan will be released from his prison and deceive multitudes into a final rebellion against the Lord and His people (Revelation 20:7–10).

If people will rebel against the perfect King, why should we expect any elected leader to enjoy universal support or accomplish everything we hope for?

The promise of no more tears, death, sorrow, or pain belongs to the new heaven and new earth, when the New Jerusalem descends from heaven and God dwells with His people (Revelation 21:1–4). We must not expect an election to deliver what only God’s final restoration can bring.

I believe this reminder is especially relevant to many Americans and Europeans:

Go and vote. Vote according to biblical convictions, without demanding a perfect candidate.

The sanctity of unborn life, God’s design for marriage and family, His creation of humanity as male and female, justice, and His enduring purposes for Israel should all inform our choices (Psalm 139:13–16; Genesis 1:27; 2:24; Romans 13:3–4; 11:28–29).

The cost of living matters. But should frustration over gas prices lead us to abandon our convictions about the value of human life, the family, or the difference between right and wrong?

Our responsibility is to remain faithful, even when we are disappointed.

“And let us not grow weary while doing good, for in due season we shall reap if we do not lose heart.” - Galatians 6:9

Only when God finally removes sin and death will sorrow and pain be gone forever.

Until then, let us choose with discernment, stand on His Word, and redeem the time, “because the days are evil” (Ephesians 5:15–16).

⚠️ Tether leads $15M funding for Mural to power AI agent payments 

👀 Tether has led a $15 million Series A funding round for New York-based Mural, supporting the financial technology company’s development of payment infrastructure for businesses and artificial intelligence agents. Mural plans to use the investment to expand internationally and develop the banking, payment and compliance services needed for software agents to conduct financial transactions.

🔔 Founded in 2022 by former Palantir engineers Sinclair Toffa and Chris Fernandes, the company provides infrastructure that businesses use to manage accounts, payment instructions, identity verification and regulatory requirements across banking networks and blockchains. Its customers include global payroll provider Deel, browser developer Opera and financial technology platform Axexo. Through Mural’s system, businesses can offer accounts holding dollars, local currencies and stablecoins without managing separate financial infrastructure for each payment method.

📌 The company reported processing $2.1 billion in payments for users across 128 countries since introducing its application programming interface in 2025. Payment volume recorded so far in 2026 is nearly six times its total for 2025. Mural has not disclosed the valuation attached to the latest funding round.
